For one case study look at how badly Google was beaten up before they hired their own cadre of lawyers and lobbyists. They didn't want to play the game, but it's not optional. You will play their game by their rules or you won't be allowed to exist.

The separation Economy and Government is the next logical step after the separation of Church and State. By forbidding government ANY interference in the realm of economy you remove the need for corporations to seek their approval before introducing a new product or service. There is no longer a power mad bureaucrat acting as gatekeeper to the future. He cannot block the needs of 100 million people just because he is in a bad mood today. Currently the EPA, FDA, FCC, CMS, and about 50 other alphabet soup agencies do this on a daily basis. It is in fact their only real function.

In a truly free market each person could decide for themselves. If you find the labor practices of Foxcom abhorrent you are free to not buy an iPhone. If you don't like Walmart's ships, do go there. IF enough people do this the corporations WILL change to give the consumers what they want. If enough people don't care, neither will the corporation.

Today what we have is a bunch of hedonistic social justice warriors - even people that say they are not. They want the cheap iPhone, but they want to hear big brother is going to whack Apple with a stick for giving children in China food. And THIS is the single most important point. Not that they are working far harder than you think they should. The fact is they are working at all. They have a job. And food. And a bed. The world is what the world is. The reality you wish existed is not the one in which the producers have to live.

It is not rocket science. Without the ability to call upon the governments unilateral and unlimited license for violence corporations are free to innovate. But they are always at the mercy of the market. Yes. The system is currently corrupt. Fatally so. But not the way most people think. Hint: That's why things are only getting worse every year. The standard of living in the US maxed out around 1972. It won't be that high again.
